questions.question: What two things are being compared in this passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an and philosophy.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an helps people notice in the world?
questions.answer: The amazing signs of Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the passage say philosophy treats many everyday things?
questions.answer: It treats them like plain, unimportant things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the creation of a human being?
questions.answer: It is a great miracle from Allah.

questions.question: What strange example does philosophy get excited about in the passage?
questions.answer: A person with an unusual body, like extra legs or heads.

questions.question: What normal blessing for babies does the passage say people should notice?
questions.answer: Their food and care from Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe that blessing for little children?
questions.answer: As a gentle and wide mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What unusual sea creature example is mentioned?
questions.answer: An insect in the sea being fed by sea plants.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring up that sea creature?
questions.answer: To show that philosophy notices odd cases more than common blessings.

questions.question: Which one is shown as richer in true wisdom: the Qur’an or philosophy?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge is the Qur’an said to give about Allah?
questions.answer: Deep understanding and wisdom about the Maker.

questions.question: What lesson should a student take from this comparison?
questions.answer: We should look carefully at Allah’s everyday blessings and signs.

questions.question: What is the main topic of this passage?
questions.answer: How the Qur’an teaches better than philosophy.

questions.question: What does the passage say covers many things in the world before the Qur’an uncovers them?
questions.answer: Habit and thinking they are just ordinary.

questions.question: After removing that cover, what does the Qur’an show people?
questions.answer: Wonderful signs and miracles in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an opens for people’s minds?
questions.answer: A treasure of knowledge.

questions.question: What does philosophy hide under “ordinary” ideas, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s amazing works in creation.

questions.question: Does the passage praise philosophy for noticing regular blessings first or rare odd things first?
questions.answer: Rare odd things first.

questions.question: In the passage, how is normal human creation treated by philosophy?
questions.answer: As if it were nothing special.

questions.question: Why is that way of looking at people shown as wrong in the passage?
questions.answer: Because a human being is a great sign of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What everyday mercy for infants is mentioned?
questions.answer: Their being provided with food.

questions.question: What bad attitude does the passage connect with ignoring that mercy?
questions.answer: Being unthankful.

questions.question: When philosophy sees an unusual creature being fed, how does it react?
questions.answer: It makes a big deal out of it.

questions.question: What final message does the passage give about philosophy next to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Philosophy is poor in true guidance, but the Qur’an is full of wisdom.

questions.question: Who is the real giver of the wonders and blessings talked about in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an do for people who think the world is only ordinary?
questions.answer: It helps them see the world’s hidden wonders.

questions.question: What kind of things does the passage say are actually miracles, even if people see them every day?
questions.answer: Created things in the universe.

questions.question: What does philosophy do instead of showing those daily miracles?
questions.answer: It passes by them without caring.

questions.question: What kind of examples does philosophy choose to point out?
questions.answer: Strange and uncommon ones.

questions.question: What example from human life is used to show this mistake?
questions.answer: It ignores normal human creation but points to a person with unusual body parts.

questions.question: What can we infer the passage wants us to feel about a normal human body?
questions.answer: Wonder and thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: What example from baby life is given to show Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: Babies regularly getting what they need to live.

questions.question: What can we learn from that example about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah is caring and merciful.

questions.question: What sea example shows philosophy’s wrong focus?
questions.answer: It notices a lonely sea insect being fed.

questions.question: Why is that focus called poor in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it misses the bigger, daily signs of Allah.

questions.question: What should a believer do after reading this comparison?
questions.answer: Take a lesson and notice Allah’s wisdom all around.

questions.question: In this passage, which source is full of wisdom: the Qur’an or philosophy?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an remove from people’s eyes and minds?
questions.answer: The idea that things are just common and usual.

questions.question: After that, how do the things in the universe appear?
questions.answer: As amazing works of Allah.

questions.question: What effect does this have on people who think deeply?
questions.answer: It draws their attention and teaches them.

questions.question: What does philosophy do to these same signs, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It hides them behind ordinary thinking.

questions.question: What kinds of things does philosophy choose as teaching examples?
questions.answer: Odd and unusual cases.

questions.question: How is a regular person’s creation described in the passage?
questions.answer: As a complete and amazing miracle.

questions.question: What is another regular event the passage says is wonderful?
questions.answer: Young children being fed.

questions.question: Why is feeding children important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows Allah’s wide mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage say philosophy puts over this mercy?
questions.answer: A cover of not being thankful.

questions.question: What does the passage say about philosophy’s knowledge next to the Qur’an’s knowledge?
questions.answer: It is weak and poor.

questions.question: What is the best response to the signs named in the passage?
questions.answer: To see them, learn from them, and thank Allah.

questions.question: What two ways of teaching are contrasted in the passage?
questions.answer: Teaching by the Qur’an and teaching by philosophy.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an treat the things people usually see every day?
questions.answer: It shows they are full of meaning and wonder.

questions.question: What does the passage say all beings in the universe really are?
questions.answer: Amazing signs of divine power.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an offer to the mind after showing these signs?
questions.answer: Endless knowledge.

questions.question: What mistake does philosophy make with common things?
questions.answer: It overlooks their greatness.

questions.question: What does philosophy admire instead?
questions.answer: Rare and strange exceptions.

questions.question: Give one human example used in the passage.
questions.answer: A normal person is ignored, but a person with an unusual body is treated as special.

questions.question: Give one example about children used in the passage.
questions.answer: Their steady feeding and care are shown as a mercy from Allah.

questions.question: Give one sea example used in the passage.
questions.answer: A sea insect being fed is treated like a big wonder.

questions.question: What do these three examples together teach?
questions.answer: Everyday blessings are greater than rare odd things.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an has in knowledge and wisdom?
questions.answer: Great richness.

questions.question: What should students remember from this passage?
questions.answer: Look at ordinary life with thankful eyes and see Allah’s signs.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to compare?
questions.answer: The results and teaching of the Qur’an and philosophy.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an reveal in the universe?
questions.answer: Surprising wonders from Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why might people miss these wonders at first?
questions.answer: Because they are used to seeing them all the time.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s mind when the Qur’an teaches them?
questions.answer: It opens to much knowledge.

questions.question: What is philosophy said to do with many clear signs in creation?
questions.answer: It hides or ignores them.

questions.question: What kinds of things does philosophy stop to notice?
questions.answer: Unusual things outside the normal pattern.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the making of a human being?
questions.answer: It is not plain; it is marvelous.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the feeding of infants?
questions.answer: It is a beautiful mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What wrong habit is shown when someone ignores daily blessings?
questions.answer: Thanklessness.

questions.question: Why is the example of the sea insect included?
questions.answer: To show how philosophy chases rare cases instead of bigger daily signs.

questions.question: In the passage, which one leads better to knowing the Maker?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What should a Muslim child do after reading this passage?
questions.answer: Notice Allah’s blessings, think about them, and be grateful.
